big: Rohan puts 10% of his ₹10 lakh portfolio in gold. A year later gold has jumped and now makes up about 15% of the portfolio. He did nothing wrong. But the mix has drifted from what he planned.

lines: So how much gold should I own?
There is no single number. A small share, planned in advance, is common. What matters is that you pick the share, and bring it back when it drifts. Education only, not advice.

note: Rebalancing means selling a bit of what grew and buying what lagged. Check taxes and costs first.

title: Gold in a portfolio
stops: Asset allocation splits money among asset classes
Rebalancing means adding more of the winner
A gold loan lets you borrow against gold
A gold loan keeps the gold with you
caps: A split among shares, bonds and gold, based on goals.
Rebalancing brings the mix back to target.
The lender holds the gold until you repay.
If you default, the lender can sell the gold.

q: Meena's gold has grown to 20% of her portfolio, against a 10% plan. What does rebalancing suggest?
why: Buying more gold would push the mix further from plan.
Doing nothing lets the mix keep drifting.
Selling everything else would break the plan altogether.
Rebalancing means selling part of what grew.

opts: The fee that a broker charges
The price of one single share
A bank's lending rate on loans
why: A broker's fee is brokerage, not allocation.
It is how a portfolio is divided among asset classes.
The price of one share is not an allocation.
A lending rate is what a bank charges on loans.

q: Dadi pledges her ornaments to a lender and gets a loan. Who holds the gold until she repays?
why: She pledged it, so it is with the lender, not her.
SEBI does not hold pledged gold for anyone.
The lender holds the pledged gold until repayment.
A jeweller nearby has no role in her loan.

q: A household has idle gold in a locker. What is gold monetisation?
opts: Melting it down at home for sale
Selling it quietly in the dark
Burying it deep in the garden
why: Gold monetisation lets idle gold earn interest.
Melting at home is unsafe and changes its form.
A sale in the dark is risky and unregulated.
Burying it earns nothing and risks loss.

pts: Choose a small, planned share of gold and stick to it.
Rebalance when the mix drifts: sell some of what grew.
A gold loan keeps your gold with the lender until you repay.
